title: GPU/renderer process crashes with EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT (0x80000003) on Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200.8655) — sandbox init failure, regression after June 2026 cumulative update
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.6.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2, Build 26200.8655 (UBR 8655). Cumulative updates KB5094135 (2026-06-09) and KB5094126 (2026-06-10) installed.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — crashes began 2026-06-16, immediately after the June 2026 cumulative update; the Electron app versions were unchanged across that boundary.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The GPU (and renderer) child process launches normally under the sandbox.

### Actual Behavior

The GPU process is killed by EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT (0x80000003 / exit_code=-2147483645) immediately on launch, **before any GPU vendor DLL is loaded**. The browser process retries 6 times within ~0.3s and then self-terminates.

Browser process log (captured with --enable-logging=stderr --v=1):

​```
[ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:996] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[WARNING:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:1438] The GPU process has crashed 1 time(s)
... (repeats up to 6 times) ...
[FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:417] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
​```

WER signature: faulting module = the app exe itself (statically-linked Chromium), exception code 80000003, identical fault offset across 70+ crash reports.

**A/B isolation (this is the key evidence):**
- Default (GPU sandbox ON): GPU process dies with 0x80000003, 6 times → browser gives up.
- `--disable-gpu-sandbox`: GPU process **survives** (falls back to swiftshader-webgl). No 0x80000003.
- For Notion, `--disable-gpu-sandbox` keeps the main process alive but the **renderer** still crashes (white screen); only `--no-sandbox` makes the renderer survive.

So: sandbox ON → child process dies during sandbox init; sandbox OFF → it lives. This points to a sandbox-init incompatibility, not a GPU driver fault (no vendor DLL is even loaded at crash time) and not third-party DLL injection (the sandboxed children can't be injected).

Google Chrome 149 on the same machine is unaffected — likely because its newer Chromium already handles the changed Windows behavior.

Hardware: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU (driver 32.0.15.9174) + AMD Radeon 610M (32.0.13034.7001), hybrid graphics laptop.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

A user on the Obsidian forum reports an identical signature (0x80000003, GPU process dies before vendor DLLs load, "GPU process isn't usable") on a different machine (AMD Radeon 780M, Windows 11 24H2), suggesting this is a broader Chromium/Electron sandbox incompatibility with recent Windows builds rather than a single-machine issue: https://forum.obsidian.md/t/gpu-process-crash-report/105321
